verdict.rationale: Stripe Invoicing documents that its invoice workflow transitions emit webhooks, which are real-time HTTPS JSON pushes, and it documents handling of failed invoice payments. That covers part of the payment-failure leg of the story. The evidence frames Invoicing around one-time invoices and never ties events to subscription renewals, upgrades or cancellations, and nothing addresses delivery reliability such as retries or ordering. Missing for 10: documented subscription-lifecycle events (renewal, upgrade, cancellation), an explicit payment-failure webhook event, webhook delivery reliability guarantees, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, every subscription state change — renewal, upgrade, payment failure, cancellation — emits a webhook or event my systems can act on reliably

citations.quote: It also lists the webhooks (A webhook is a real-time push notification sent to your application as a JSON payload through HTTPS requests) that are emitted by the endpoint
If the invoice becomes overdue, or payment on the invoice fails, Stripe can automatically send reminders or retry the payment for you.
